THE WARRANTIES IN SECTION 5.1 ARE THE EXCLUSIVE WARRANTIES FROM IBM. THEY REPLACE ALL OTHER WARRANTIES, INCLUDING, WITHOUT LIMITATION, THE IMPLIED WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY, SATISFACTORY QUALITY, AND FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

Rule:
ID: LD
Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: Service credits to us are welcome; liquidated damages against us are not.
Severity: high
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.
Position — fallback:
Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.

Liquidated damages exceeding the remaining contract value or triggered by minor breaches.

Identify liquidated damages, penalties, minimum fees on termination, "shall pay … as liquidated damages". Flag only when Customer pays. Service credits or LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant.

Redline guidance:
Delete the Customer-payable LD; if an early-termination fee is unavoidable, cap it at 3 months' fees.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.

Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.

Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.

Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.
Severity: high
Category: assignment
Position — preferred:
Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) and never to a Customer competitor; no Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control.

Position — fallback:
Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice; consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.
Position — walk-away:
Blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, or a Vendor right to terminate or re-price on Customer's change of control.

Detection guidance:
"may not assign", "change of control", "deemed an assignment", consent standards. Determine whether the restriction binds Customer symmetrically and whether change-of-control triggers any Vendor right.

Redline guidance:
Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: LD
Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: Service credits to us are welcome; liquidated damages against us are not.
Severity: high
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.
Position — fallback:
Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.
Position — walk-away:
Liquidated damages exceeding the remaining contract value or triggered by minor breaches.

Identify liquidated damages, penalties, minimum fees on termination, "shall pay … as liquidated damages". Flag only when Customer pays. Service credits or LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant.

Redline guidance:
Delete the Customer-payable LD; if an early-termination fee is unavoidable, cap it at 3 months' fees.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

input.quote: Customer will not assign this Agreement or any of its rights hereunder without the prior written consent of IBM, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer may assign this Agreement to a successor organization by merger, consolidation or acquisition.
input.rationale: § 14.10 restricts only Customer: we need IBM's consent to assign (with a narrow successor carve-out limited to merger, consolidation or acquisition, and no affiliate or asset-sale carve-out), while IBM's own right to assign is entirely unrestricted, with no consent requirement and no bar on assignment to a competitor of ours. That fails the fallback, which requires mutuality — a mutual right to assign to successors and a reasonable-consent standard for other assignments. The redline adds the affiliate/asset-sale carve-out for us and subjects IBM's assignment to our consent (not unreasonably withheld) with a competitor bar, reaching the preferred position with a single-sentence change. Positively, there is no change-of-control provision anywhere in the Agreement and no IBM termination or re-pricing right on our change of control, so no walk-away issue arises; IBM's subcontracting right in § 14.8 is left untouched.

proposal.summary: Add affiliate/asset-sale carve-out for Customer and make IBM's assignment subject to our consent, with no assignment to our competitors.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We expanded the carve-out so we may assign to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets without consent, and made IBM's assignment subject to our consent (not unreasonably withheld) and never to a competitor of ours. Our playbook requires this symmetry; as a fallback we can accept a mutual right to assign to successors on written notice with consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.
Severity: high
Category: assignment
Position — preferred:
Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) and never to a Customer competitor; no Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control.

Position — fallback:
Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice; consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.
Position — walk-away:
Blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, or a Vendor right to terminate or re-price on Customer's change of control.

Detection guidance:
"may not assign", "change of control", "deemed an assignment", consent standards. Determine whether the restriction binds Customer symmetrically and whether change-of-control triggers any Vendor right.

Redline guidance:
Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

input.quote: IBM grants Customer a nonexclusive, revocable license to use the Base Components solely in connection with the Services as provided under this Agreement.
input.rationale: § 12.1 is the only grant clause. It is expressly "revocable" with no stated standard, so IBM may withdraw the licence at will — walk-away territory under the rule. It also names only Customer, with no coverage for Affiliates or Subcontractors acting on our behalf and no notice mechanic to add them, and § 14.17 confirms no other rights are granted by implication. The transferability limb of the fallback is satisfied by § 14.10, which permits assignment to a successor by merger, consolidation or acquisition, so we left that untouched. Redline makes the minimal fix: adds Affiliates and Subcontractors acting on our behalf, and limits revocation to termination for our uncured material breach.

proposal.summary: Extend the Base Components licence to Customer's Affiliates and Subcontractors and remove IBM's at-will revocation right
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We extended the Base Components licence to our Affiliates and to Subcontractors acting on our behalf, and replaced the at-will revocation right with revocation only on termination for our uncured material breach, so the licence cannot be pulled while we are paying for the Services. If helpful, we can accept affiliate coverage on written notice instead.

ops.newText: IBM grants Customer, its Affiliates and its Subcontractors acting on Customer's behalf a nonexclusive license to use the Base Components solely in connection with the Services as provided under this Agreement. Such license is irrevocable during the term of the applicable Services, and may be revoked or terminated by IBM only upon termination of this Agreement or the applicable Service Option Attachment for Customer's uncured material breach.

ID: LICENSE
Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.
Severity: high
Category: licence

Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

**Finding: deviation (§ 14.10 Assignment, p0188)** — redline validated and submitted.

- **Issue:** The restriction is one-way. We need IBM's consent to assign, with a narrow successor carve-out (merger, consolidation or acquisition only — no affiliate or sale-of-assets carve-out), while IBM's ability to assign is wholly unrestricted, with no consent requirement and no bar on assignment to one of our competitors. That asymmetry fails even the fallback, which requires mutuality and a reasonable-consent standard.
- **Fix (preferred position, one sentence):** carve out assignments to affiliates and to successors by merger, consolidation, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; and subject IBM's assignment to our prior written consent (not unreasonably withheld), never to a Customer competitor.
- **Not flagged:** there is no change-of-control provision anywhere in the Agreement and no IBM termination or re-pricing right on our change of control, so no walk-away trigger; IBM's § 14.8 subcontracting right is left intact.

messages.content:
Rule:
ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.
Severity: high
Category: assignment
Position — preferred:
Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) and never to a Customer competitor; no Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control.

Position — fallback:
Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice; consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.
Position — walk-away:
Blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, or a Vendor right to terminate or re-price on Customer's change of control.

Detection guidance:
"may not assign", "change of control", "deemed an assignment", consent standards. Determine whether the restriction binds Customer symmetrically and whether change-of-control triggers any Vendor right.

Redline guidance:
Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
§ 14.10 restricts only Customer: we need IBM's consent to assign (with a narrow successor carve-out limited to merger, consolidation or acquisition, and no affiliate or asset-sale carve-out), while IBM's own right to assign is entirely unrestricted, with no consent requirement and no bar on assignment to a competitor of ours. That fails the fallback, which requires mutuality — a mutual right to assign to successors and a reasonable-consent standard for other assignments. The redline adds the affiliate/asset-sale carve-out for us and subjects IBM's assignment to our consent (not unreasonably withheld) with a competitor bar, reaching the preferred position with a single-sentence change. Positively, there is no change-of-control provision anywhere in the Agreement and no IBM termination or re-pricing right on our change of control, so no walk-away issue arises; IBM's subcontracting right in § 14.8 is left untouched.

Original paragraphs:
p0188: Customer will not assign this Agreement or any of its rights hereunder without the prior written consent of IBM, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer may assign this Agreement to a successor organization by merger, consolidation or acquisition. Any attempted assignment in violation of the foregoing will be void. In any permitted assignment, Customer will remain liable for its obligations hereunder.

Resolved definitions:
Customer: Under this e-business Hosting Agreement ("Agreement") between International Business Machines Corporation ("IBM") and Bluefly, Inc. ("Customer"), IBM will provide Web hosting and related services ("Services") to Customer. The Agreement includes these terms and conditions and the documents referenced herein ("Base Terms"), e-business hosting services order forms accepted by IBM ("Order Forms"), and the following attachments:

Rendered redline:
p0188: Customer will not assign this Agreement or any of its rights hereunder without the prior written consent of IBM, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer may assign this Agreement without consent to an affiliate or to a successor organization by merger, consolidation, acquisition or sale of substantially all of its assets. IBM will not assign this Agreement without Customer's prior written consent, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld, and in no event to a competitor of Customer. Any attempted assignment in violation of the foregoing will be void. In any permitted assignment, Customer will remain liable for its obligations hereunder.

Comment:
[Playbook] We expanded the carve-out so we may assign to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets without consent, and made IBM's assignment subject to our consent (not unreasonably withheld) and never to a competitor of ours. Our playbook requires this symmetry; as a fallback we can accept a mutual right to assign to successors on written notice with consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.

content.text:
**Finding: deviation (§ 12.1 License)**

The grant in § 12.1 fails the fallback on two material terms:

1. **Revocability** — the licence is expressly "revocable" with no standard attached, meaning IBM can withdraw our right to use the Base Components at its discretion. That is explicit walk-away territory under the rule.
2. **Permitted users** — only "Customer" is named. Neither Affiliates (defined at p0015) nor Subcontractors (defined at p0031) are covered, and § 14.17 (Limitation of Licenses) forecloses any implied extension, so there is no path to add them.

Transferability is already acceptable: § 14.10 permits assignment to a successor by merger, consolidation or acquisition, so I did not touch it (and did not double-flag it).

Redline validated (ok:true) and submitted — it adds Affiliates and Subcontractors acting on our behalf, and limits revocation to termination for our uncured material breach, with affiliate-coverage-on-notice offered as the fallback in the comment.

Rule:
ID: LICENSE
Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.
Severity: high
Category: licence
Position — preferred:
Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Position — fallback:
Affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
Position — walk-away:
Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion; affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them.
Detection guidance:
Find the grant clause: "non-exclusive, non-transferable", "revocable", "solely for Customer's internal use", whether affiliates/contractors are named, term of the licence.

Redline guidance:
Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
§ 12.1 is the only grant clause. It is expressly "revocable" with no stated standard, so IBM may withdraw the licence at will — walk-away territory under the rule. It also names only Customer, with no coverage for Affiliates or Subcontractors acting on our behalf and no notice mechanic to add them, and § 14.17 confirms no other rights are granted by implication. The transferability limb of the fallback is satisfied by § 14.10, which permits assignment to a successor by merger, consolidation or acquisition, so we left that untouched. Redline makes the minimal fix: adds Affiliates and Subcontractors acting on our behalf, and limits revocation to termination for our uncured material breach.

Original paragraphs:
p0149: IBM grants Customer a nonexclusive, revocable license to use the Base Components solely in connection with the Services as provided under this Agreement. Customer agrees not to download or otherwise copy, reverse assemble, reverse compile, or otherwise translate the software
p0202: Each of us grants only the licenses expressly specified herein. No other licenses or rights (including licenses or rights under patents) are granted.
p0188: Customer will not assign this Agreement or any of its rights hereunder without the prior written consent of IBM, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer may assign this Agreement to a successor organization by merger, consolidation or acquisition. Any attempted assignment in violation of the foregoing will be void. In any permitted assignment, Customer will remain liable for its obligations hereunder.

Resolved definitions:
Customer: Under this e-business Hosting Agreement ("Agreement") between International Business Machines Corporation ("IBM") and Bluefly, Inc. ("Customer"), IBM will provide Web hosting and related services ("Services") to Customer. The Agreement includes these terms and conditions and the documents referenced herein ("Base Terms"), e-business hosting services order forms accepted by IBM ("Order Forms"), and the following attachments:

Rendered redline:
p0149: IBM grants Customer, its Affiliates and its Subcontractors acting on Customer's behalf a nonexclusive license to use the Base Components solely in connection with the Services as provided under this Agreement. Such license is irrevocable during the term of the applicable Services, and may be revoked or terminated by IBM only upon termination of this Agreement or the applicable Service Option Attachment for Customer's uncured material breach. Customer agrees not to download or otherwise copy, reverse assemble, reverse compile, or otherwise translate the software

Comment:
[Playbook] We extended the Base Components licence to our Affiliates and to Subcontractors acting on our behalf, and replaced the at-will revocation right with revocation only on termination for our uncured material breach, so the licence cannot be pulled while we are paying for the Services. If helpful, we can accept affiliate coverage on written notice instead.

input.quote: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no express liquidated damages or penalty clause, but Section 3.4(b) makes Customer pay "early termination charges" on convenience termination in an amount defined only by an open cross-reference to Attachment A and the Service Option Attachments (neither of which caps the amount, and Attachment A is not part of this document). Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (Section 3.4(b), ¶p0046).**

- **What I found:** No express liquidated damages or penalty clause exists (search for "liquidated damages" returned nothing). However, Section 3.4(b) requires Customer to pay "early termination charges" on convenience termination, with the amount set only by an open cross-reference to Attachment A and the Service Option Attachments — neither of which is in this document or contains a cap.
- **Why it fails:** An uncapped Customer-payable termination amount does not meet the fallback (early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees), and unbounded it risks the walk-away scenario of exceeding remaining contract value.
- **Redline (validated, ok:true):** Added a proviso capping aggregate early termination charges at three (3) months' recurring Charges for the terminated Services and making them Customer's sole liability for the termination — consistent with the seed-ld precedent.
- **Not flagged:** Section 3.5's accrued-payments-become-due language is ordinary; Section 3.3 already bars IBM from recovering early termination charges where it breached (in our favour); Section 4.2's "late payment fees" belongs to the payment-terms rule, not double-flagged here.

You are an independent verifier of one proposed contract finding.
Judge the proposal against the supplied playbook rule, original paragraphs, resolved definitions, deterministic checks, rendered redline, and comment.
Do not rely on hidden drafter reasoning. Fail invalid, directionally wrong, or rule-incomplete edits.
Deterministic checks are heuristics (regular expressions and a changed-character ratio), not verdicts: a failed regex may simply be a phrasing variant, and a high changed-character ratio is acceptable when the rule genuinely requires rewriting the clause (for example replacing a governing-law sentence or deleting a take-or-pay obligation). Weigh them as evidence and decide on substance: does the redline reach the playbook position with the smallest edit that does so, and is the comment accurate?
The claimed status matters: for a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment is expected, and you should pass when the cited text supports compliance. Fail a deviation finding whose cited clause already meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms (the playbook's classification semantics) — a redline that merely upgrades an acceptable fallback to preferred wording is over-flagging. Compliant findings are retained as internal evaluation evidence, not raised as negotiation issues. For deviation or missing findings, require an actionable valid proposal.
Return a concise verdict with actionable reasons.

messages.content:
Rule:
ID: LD
Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: Service credits to us are welcome; liquidated damages against us are not.
Severity: high
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.
Position — fallback:
Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.
Position — walk-away:
Liquidated damages exceeding the remaining contract value or triggered by minor breaches.
Detection guidance:
Identify liquidated damages, penalties, minimum fees on termination, "shall pay … as liquidated damages". Flag only when Customer pays. Service credits or LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant.

Redline guidance:
Delete the Customer-payable LD; if an early-termination fee is unavoidable, cap it at 3 months' fees.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
The Agreement contains no express liquidated damages or penalty clause, but Section 3.4(b) makes Customer pay "early termination charges" on convenience termination in an amount defined only by an open cross-reference to Attachment A and the Service Option Attachments (neither of which caps the amount, and Attachment A is not part of this document). That is a Customer-payable termination amount with no ceiling, so it fails the fallback position of an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees; unbounded, it could approach or exceed remaining contract value (walk-away territory). Because a termination charge is a normal part of the bargain in a facilities-services deal with a broad convenience-termination right, we took the fallback rather than deleting the charge: the redline caps aggregate early termination charges at three (3) months' recurring Charges for the terminated Services and makes them Customer's sole liability for the termination. Section 3.5's accrued-payment obligation is ordinary and not flagged, and Section 3.3's carve-out (no early termination charges where IBM breached) already runs in our favour.

Original paragraphs:
p0046: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.
p0049: Upon the date of termination, all Customer payment obligations accrued hereunder through the date of termination will become due and payable. The termination of selected Service Option Attachments will not affect Customer's obligation to pay charges under other Service Option Attachments.

Resolved definitions:
Customer: Under this e-business Hosting Agreement ("Agreement") between International Business Machines Corporation ("IBM") and Bluefly, Inc. ("Customer"), IBM will provide Web hosting and related services ("Services") to Customer. The Agreement includes these terms and conditions and the documents referenced herein ("Base Terms"), e-business hosting services order forms accepted by IBM ("Order Forms"), and the following attachments:
Service Option Attachments: c. all other applicable attachments referenced in the Order Forms for Services options selected by Customer ("Service Option Attachments").

Rendered redline:
p0046: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments; provided that Customer's aggregate early termination charges for any such termination will not exceed three (3) months' recurring Charges for the terminated Services and will be Customer's sole liability arising from such termination.

Comment:
[Playbook] Our playbook does not accept liquidated amounts payable by us, so we have capped the early termination charges cross-referenced to Attachment A at three months' recurring Charges and made them the sole amount due on convenience termination. We are happy to keep the charge itself, but it needs a defined ceiling rather than an open cross-reference.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

reasons: The cited grant (p0149) is expressly 'revocable' with no standard and names only Customer, with no affiliate/contractor coverage and no notice path to add them — it fails the fallback on two material terms and touches walk-away territory, so 'deviation' is the correct classification.

The redline is directionally correct and actionable: it deletes 'revocable', extends the grant to Affiliates and Subcontractors acting on Customer's behalf, and confines revocation to termination for Customer's uncured material breach, matching the rule's preferred position for subscription-style licences.

The rationale correctly declines to redline transferability because § 14.10 (p0188) already permits assignment to a successor by merger, consolidation or acquisition — avoiding over-flagging an already-satisfied limb.

The advisory changed-character ratio (0.701) is justified here: removing at-will revocation necessarily requires inserting a revocation standard, and the added sentence is confined to that purpose; the balance of the paragraph (copying/reverse-engineering restrictions) is preserved verbatim.

Comment is concise, in first person plural, states what changed and why, and offers the fallback (affiliate coverage on written notice). Minor, non-blocking point: 'Affiliates' and 'Subcontractors acting on Customer's behalf' may not be defined terms for the Customer side in this agreement, so a definitional hook or lowercase usage could be confirmed at drafting.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

paragraphs.text: 5.3 Security
a. Customer acknowledges that IBM does not control the transfer of data over telecommunications facilities, including the Internet.

b. Subject to the other disclaimers contained herein, IBM will implement the security features specified herein, including the IBM perform security obligations identified in Section 8.0 of the Facilities Services Service Option Attachment. However, IBM does not warrant secure operation of the Services or that it will be able to prevent third party disruptions of the e-business Hosting Environment or Customer Components.

c. Customer acknowledges that IBM offers numerous security options, specified in Service Option Attachments. Customer is responsible for selecting on Order Forms the set of security options that it determines meet Customer's needs.
d. Customer agrees that IBM shall have no liability for any provision of security-related services or advice that IBM may voluntarily provide outside the scope of selected Service Option Attachments.
14.12 Risk of Loss
Risk of loss for all Base Components shall at all times remain with IBM. Risk of loss for all Customer Components shall at all times remain with Customer.
14.18 Data Protection

You agree to allow International Business Machines Corporation and entities within its Enterprise to store and use your contact information, including names, phone numbers, and e-mail addresses, anywhere they do business. Such information will be processed and used in connection with our business relationship, and may be provided to contractors, Business Partners, and assignees of IBM Corp. and entities within its Enterprise for uses consistent with their collective business activities, including communicating with you (for example, for processing orders, for promotions, and for marketing research). For personal information processed by IBM on your behalf as part of the Services, IBM will act in accordance with your instructions by following such processing and security obligations as are contained in this Agreement. You also confirm that you are solely responsible for ensuring that any processing and security obligations comply with applicable data protection laws. Your contact information shall not be considered personal information processed on your behalf.

reasons: The cited § 14.10 binds only Customer: Customer needs IBM's consent (with a narrow merger/consolidation/acquisition carve-out) while IBM's assignment is entirely unrestricted — no consent standard and no competitor bar. That asymmetry fails the fallback, which contemplates a mutual right to assign to successors and a reasonable-consent standard for other assignments, so the deviation classification is correct rather than over-flagging an acceptable fallback.

The redline reaches the preferred position with a targeted edit: it keeps the original consent sentence, voiding sentence and continuing-liability sentence intact, widens the Customer carve-out to affiliates and sale of substantially all assets, and adds one sentence subjecting IBM's assignment to Customer's consent (not unreasonably withheld) with a competitor bar. The failed 'minimal edit' heuristic (0.656) reflects the added mutuality sentence, which the rule expressly requires ('Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer'); no unnecessary text was disturbed.

Direction is correct and pro-Customer; nothing in the edit worsens our position, and the redline is legally coherent (the existing 'void' and 'Customer will remain liable' language still reads sensibly).

The comment is accurate, in the required first-person plural tone with the [Playbook] prefix, explains both changes and offers the fallback; the rationale correctly notes the absence of any change-of-control termination or re-pricing right, so no walk-away issue is overstated, and § 14.8 subcontracting is left alone (no double-flagging).

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

input.quote: a. it will perform the Services using reasonable care and skill and in accordance with the applicable Service Option Attachments
input.rationale: Section 5.1 gives only a care-and-skill/qualified-personnel warranty plus an authority rep and a compliance-with-laws covenant. There is no conformance warranty for Materials or Services output, no warranty period, and no remedy (re-performance, repair, replacement or refund), and Section 5.4(c) affirmatively provides all Materials "AS IS" while 5.2 makes 5.1 exclusive — so the disclaimer swallows any conformance protection. That fails even the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with the stated remedies) and approaches the walk-away position for deliverables. Redline adds a 90-day conformance and no-malicious-code warranty for Materials with a repair/re-performance/refund remedy and carves the express warranties out of the "AS IS" disclaimer; the existing care-and-skill language already satisfies the professional/workmanlike element and is left intact.

proposal.summary: Add a 90-day conformance warranty for Materials with a repair/re-perform/refund remedy and carve the express warranties out of the "AS IS" disclaimer.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] IBM's warranty covers only care and skill, with no conformance warranty for Materials, no warranty period and no remedy, and Section 5.4(c) then puts all Materials "AS IS". We have added a 90-day conformance and no-malicious-code warranty with a repair, re-performance or refund remedy, and carved the express warranties out of the disclaimer so they are not swallowed.

ops.text: c. for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Material delivered by IBM will conform in all material respects to its documentation and to the specifications in the applicable Service Option Attachment, and will not contain any virus, malicious or disabling code.

Customer's remedy for breach of the warranties in this Section 5.1 is, at IBM's option, re-performance of the non-conforming Services, repair or replacement of the non-conforming Material, or a refund of the charges paid for the non-conforming Services or Material.

ops.newText: EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY WARRANTED IN SECTION 5.1, IBM PROVIDES ALL MATERIALS AND ALL NON-IBM SERVICES

- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

input.quote: If not specified, Materials will be considered Type II Materials.
input.rationale: Section 7 allocates IP in delivered Materials. Type I Materials are Customer-owned, but the default for any Material not expressly designated is Type II — i.e. IBM (or a third party) holds all right, title and interest even in works created during the Service performance period specifically for us. The only licence back is "irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, paid-up ... to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, and distribute, within Customer's Enterprise only", with no right to modify/prepare derivative works and no right to sublicense. That fails both the preferred position (Customer owns work product created for it) and the fallback (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business) on material terms. There is also no statement anywhere that we retain rights in our Content, Customer Components or data; §14.17 grants only expressly specified licences, so silence leaves our data ownership unconfirmed. No assignment of Customer IP or data to IBM and no joint ownership exists, so this is not walk-away territory. Redline: flip the default to Type I, extend the Type II licence to modification and sublicensing for our business purposes, and add a Customer Content/data ownership sentence. The broad licence we grant IBM in Type I Materials (p0084) is noted but not flagged, as it is not an assignment.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

ID: INSURANCE

Kind: missing

E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.

No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.

Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).

Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.

Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.quote: IBM reserves the right to investigate potential violations of the representations and warranties in Subsection 11.2(b).
input.rationale: § 11.3 is the only right in the Agreement to examine Customer's use of the Services and Content (compliance with the Acceptable Use Policy under § 11.2(b)); there is no other audit, inspection or verification clause (no hits for audit/inspect/verify/records). As drafted the investigation right is unlimited in frequency, requires no advance notice to Customer (the notice in p0137 is only a best-efforts attempt and applies solely before IBM restricts access or removes Content, not before investigating), allocates no cost, imposes no confidentiality on investigators and does not exclude access to Customer systems. That is unlimited and unannounced examination, i.e. walk-away territory, so it fails the fallback on frequency, notice and cost. Redline adopts the fallback (once per twelve months, 15 days' notice, IBM's cost unless underpayment exceeds 10%, no system access) rather than the preferred 30-day/5% formulation, because a 30-day wait would be disproportionate in the context of suspected unlawful Content on IBM-hosted infrastructure.

ops.oldText: IBM reserves the right to investigate potential violations of the representations and warranties in Subsection 11.2(b).
ops.newText: IBM reserves the right to investigate potential violations of the representations and warranties in Subsection 11.2(b), provided that any such investigation will be conducted no more than once in any twelve (12) month period, upon at least fifteen (15) days' prior written notice to Customer, during normal business hours, by an independent investigator bound by written obligations of confidentiality, at IBM's cost unless the investigation reveals an underpayment by Customer exceeding ten percent (10%) of amounts due, and without direct or remote access to Customer's systems or Customer Components.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added the standard guardrails on investigations of our use: no more than once in any twelve-month period, on fifteen (15) days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent investigator under confidentiality, at IBM's cost unless an underpayment above 10% is found, and with no access to our systems. Our playbook does not permit unlimited or unannounced audits or vendor access to Customer systems; we are happy to discuss a shorter notice period where IBM has a good-faith, documented suspicion of unlawful Content.
proposal.summary: Add frequency, notice, cost and no-system-access limits to IBM's investigation right in § 11.3

input.rationale: § 11.3 is the only right in the Agreement to examine Customer's use of the Services and Content (compliance with the Acceptable Use Policy under § 11.2(b)); there is no other audit, inspection or verification clause (no hits for audit/inspect/verify/records). As drafted the investigation right is unlimited in frequency, requires no advance notice to Customer (the notice in p0137 is only a best-efforts attempt and applies solely before IBM restricts access or removes Content, not before investigating), allocates no cost, imposes no confidentiality on investigators and does not exclude access to Customer systems. That is unlimited and unannounced examination, i.e. walk-away territory, so it fails the fallback on frequency, notice and cost. Redline adopts the fallback (once per twelve months, 15 days' notice, IBM's cost unless underpayment exceeds 10%, no system access) rather than the preferred 30-day/5% formulation, because a 30-day wait would be disproportionate in the context of suspected unlawful Content on IBM-hosted infrastructure.

content.text:
**Finding: deviation (WARRANTY)** — submitted.

- **What the document says:** § 5.1 warrants only that IBM will perform Services "using reasonable care and skill" with qualified personnel, plus a corporate-authority rep and a covenant to comply with laws applicable to IBM's business. § 5.2 makes those the exclusive warranties, and § 5.4(c) provides all Materials "AS IS."
- **Why it fails the fallback:** no conformance warranty for Materials/Services output, no warranty duration, and no remedy (re-performance, repair, replacement or refund) — and the "AS IS" disclaimer swallows any residual protection for deliverables.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** new § 5.1(c) 90-day conformance + no-malicious-code warranty for Materials; a remedy sentence after the compliance covenant (IBM's option: re-performance, repair/replacement, or refund of charges paid); and "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY WARRANTED IN SECTION 5.1" carve-out at the front of § 5.4(c). The existing care-and-skill language already meets the professional/workmanlike element and was left untouched.
