Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.


Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 5.1 gives only a care-and-skill/qualified-personnel warranty plus an authority rep and a compliance-with-laws covenant. There is no conformance warranty for Materials or Services output, no warranty period, and no remedy (re-performance, repair, replacement or refund), and Section 5.4(c) affirmatively provides all Materials "AS IS" while 5.2 makes 5.1 exclusive — so the disclaimer swallows any conformance protection. That fails even the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with the stated remedies) and approaches the walk-away position for deliverables. Redline adds a 90-day conformance and no-malicious-code warranty for Materials with a repair/re-performance/refund remedy and carves the express warranties out of the "AS IS" disclaimer; the existing care-and-skill language already satisfies the professional/workmanlike element and is left intact.

Original paragraphs:
p0061: a. it will perform the Services using reasonable care and skill and in accordance with the applicable Service Option Attachments (which means the degree of knowledge, skill and judgment customarily exercised by members of the applicable profession with respect to work of a similar nature); and that it will provide Customer with competent, fully trained, fully qualified and responsible personnel to perform the Services; and
p0062: b. it has the requisite corporate power and authority to execute, deliver and perform its obligations under this Agreement.
p0063: IBM covenants that it will comply with the laws applicable to IBM's business.
p0065: THE WARRANTIES IN SECTION 5.1 ARE THE EXCLUSIVE WARRANTIES FROM IBM. THEY REPLACE ALL OTHER WARRANTIES, INCLUDING, WITHOUT LIMITATION, THE IMPLIED WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY, SATISFACTORY QUALITY, AND FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.
p0074: c. IBM PROVIDES ALL MATERIALS AND ALL NON-IBM SERVICES, PRODUCTS, DATA, APPARATUS AND SOFTWARE "AS IS", WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND, INCLUDING, WITHOUT LIMITATION, THE IMPLIED WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY, SATISFACTORY QUALITY, AND FITNESS FOR&sbsp;A PARTICULAR PURPOSE. Non-IBM suppliers may provide their own warranties to you.

Resolved definitions:
Customer: Under this e-business Hosting Agreement ("Agreement") between International Business Machines Corporation ("IBM") and Bluefly, Inc. ("Customer"), IBM will provide Web hosting and related services ("Services") to Customer. The Agreement includes these terms and conditions and the documents referenced herein ("Base Terms"), e-business hosting services order forms accepted by IBM ("Order Forms"), and the following attachments:
Service Option Attachments: c. all other applicable attachments referenced in the Order Forms for Services options selected by Customer ("Service Option Attachments").

Rendered redline:
p0062: b. it has the requisite corporate power and authority to execute, deliver and perform its obligations under this Agreement.
c. for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Material delivered by IBM will conform in all material respects to its documentation and to the specifications in the applicable Service Option Attachment, and will not contain any virus, malicious or disabling code.
p0063: IBM covenants that it will comply with the laws applicable to IBM's business.
Customer's remedy for breach of the warranties in this Section 5.1 is, at IBM's option, re-performance of the non-conforming Services, repair or replacement of the non-conforming Material, or a refund of the charges paid for the non-conforming Services or Material.
p0074: c. EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY WARRANTED IN SECTION 5.1, IBM PROVIDES ALL MATERIALS AND ALL NON-IBM SERVICES, PRODUCTS, DATA, APPARATUS AND SOFTWARE "AS IS", WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND, INCLUDING, WITHOUT LIMITATION, THE IMPLIED WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY, SATISFACTORY QUALITY, AND FITNESS FOR&sbsp;A PARTICULAR PURPOSE. Non-IBM suppliers may provide their own warranties to you.

Comment:
[Playbook] IBM's warranty covers only care and skill, with no conformance warranty for Materials, no warranty period and no remedy, and Section 5.4(c) then puts all Materials "AS IS". We have added a 90-day conformance and no-malicious-code warranty with a repair, re-performance or refund remedy, and carved the express warranties out of the disclaimer so they are not swallowed.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

**Finding submitted: deviation (IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data).**

What I found:
- **§7.0 Materials (p0082–p0086)** is the operative IP allocation. Type I Materials are Customer-owned, but the **default for undesignated Materials is Type II**, meaning IBM owns even work product created for us during the Service performance period.
- The **Type II licence back** is "irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, paid-up ... within Customer's Enterprise only" — **no right to modify/create derivative works and no right to sublicense**, which fails the fallback position, not just the preferred one.
- **No Customer Data / Content ownership statement** anywhere; combined with §14.17 (only expressly granted licences), our retained rights in Content and Customer Components are unstated. There is no assignment of our IP/data to IBM and no joint ownership, so this is not walk-away.

Redline (validated ok:true, preferred level, 3 minimal ops):
1. p0082 — flip the default to Type I for Materials created during the Service performance period.
2. p0085 — make the Type II licence perpetual and add modify/derivative works and sublicensing rights for our business purposes (replacing the "Enterprise only" restriction).
3. New §7.e — confirm we retain all right, title and interest in Content, Customer Components and our data, with no assignment to IBM.

The broad licence we grant IBM in Type I Materials (p0084) is noted in the rationale but not flagged, since it is a licence rather than an assignment.

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 7 allocates IP in delivered Materials. Type I Materials are Customer-owned, but the default for any Material not expressly designated is Type II — i.e. IBM (or a third party) holds all right, title and interest even in works created during the Service performance period specifically for us. The only licence back is "irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, paid-up ... to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, and distribute, within Customer's Enterprise only", with no right to modify/prepare derivative works and no right to sublicense. That fails both the preferred position (Customer owns work product created for it) and the fallback (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business) on material terms. There is also no statement anywhere that we retain rights in our Content, Customer Components or data; §14.17 grants only expressly specified licences, so silence leaves our data ownership unconfirmed. No assignment of Customer IP or data to IBM and no joint ownership exists, so this is not walk-away territory. Redline: flip the default to Type I, extend the Type II licence to modification and sublicensing for our business purposes, and add a Customer Content/data ownership sentence. Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
§ 11.3 is the only right in the Agreement to examine Customer's use of the Services and Content (compliance with the Acceptable Use Policy under § 11.2(b)); there is no other audit, inspection or verification clause (no hits for audit/inspect/verify/records). As drafted the investigation right is unlimited in frequency, requires no advance notice to Customer (the notice in p0137 is only a best-efforts attempt and applies solely before IBM restricts access or removes Content, not before investigating), allocates no cost, imposes no confidentiality on investigators and does not exclude access to Customer systems. That is unlimited and unannounced examination, i.e. walk-away territory, so it fails the fallback on frequency, notice and cost. Redline adopts the fallback (once per twelve months, 15 days' notice, IBM's cost unless underpayment exceeds 10%, no system access) rather than the preferred 30-day/5% formulation, because a 30-day wait would be disproportionate in the context of suspected unlawful Content on IBM-hosted infrastructure.

Original paragraphs:
p0132: IBM reserves the right to investigate potential violations of the representations and warranties in Subsection 11.2(b). If IBM reasonably determines that a breach of any such warranty has occurred, then IBM may, in its sole and reasonable discretion:
p0137: Except in an emergency or as may otherwise be required by law, before undertaking the activities in Subsection 11.3(a) or 11.3(b), IBM will attempt to notify Customer by any reasonably practical means under the circumstances, such as, without limitation, by telephone or e-mail.

("Customer"), IBM will provide Web hosting and related services ("Services") to Customer. The Agreement includes these terms and conditions and the documents referenced herein ("Base Terms"), e-business hosting services order forms accepted by IBM ("Order Forms"), and the following attachments:

p0132: IBM reserves the right to investigate potential violations of the representations and warranties in Subsection 11.2(b), provided that any such investigation will be conducted no more than once in any twelve (12) month period, upon at least fifteen (15) days' prior written notice to Customer, during normal business hours, by an independent investigator bound by written obligations of confidentiality, at IBM's cost unless the investigation reveals an underpayment by Customer exceeding ten percent (10%) of amounts due, and without direct or remote access to Customer's systems or Customer Components. If IBM reasonably determines that a breach of any such warranty has occurred, then IBM may, in its sole and reasonable discretion:

Comment:
[Playbook] We added the standard guardrails on investigations of our use: no more than once in any twelve-month period, on fifteen (15) days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent investigator under confidentiality, at IBM's cost unless an underpayment above 10% is found, and with no access to our systems. Our playbook does not permit unlimited or unannounced audits or vendor access to Customer systems; we are happy to discuss a shorter notice period where IBM has a good-faith, documented suspicion of unlawful Content.

Charges under § 4.1 are payable only for Services specified in Service Option Attachments and Order Forms (one-time, installment, recurring or usage), i.e. for ordered or actual usage only, which is the preferred position. § 11.5 (Capacity Planning) allocates capacity-planning responsibility to Customer but imposes no committed capacity or volume floor, and § 3.4 lets Customer terminate the Agreement or any Service Option Attachment for convenience on one month's notice. input.quote: Risk of loss for all Base Components shall at all times remain with IBM. Risk of loss for all Customer Components shall at all times remain with Customer.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no insurance clause anywhere: a search for "insurance" returns nothing, and the sections that might carry a coverage undertaking (5.3 Security, 14.12 Risk of Loss, 14.18 Data Protection) address only security features, allocation of risk of loss and data processing, with no obligation to maintain coverage. IBM is a hosting vendor that operates the e-business Hosting Environment and processes personal information on Customer's behalf, so this falls squarely within the rule (and no coverage for a vendor processing personal data is walk-away territory). We therefore insert the preferred short insurance paragraph (CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M, workers' compensation, certificates on request) as new Section 14.12A in the general provisions; the E&O 1M / cyber 2M fallback remains available if IBM pushes back on limits.

ops.text: Insurance

IBM shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000 covering IBM's processing of Customer data; and workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable law. IBM shall provide certificates of insurance to Customer on request.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added a standard insurance provision, as our playbook requires coverage for vendors that host and process our data; certificates are provided on request only. If helpful, we can discuss reduced cyber limits.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.


Claimed finding status: missing

Finding rationale:
The Agreement contains no insurance clause anywhere: a search for "insurance" returns nothing, and the sections that might carry a coverage undertaking (5.3 Security, 14.12 Risk of Loss, 14.18 Data Protection) address only security features, allocation of risk of loss and data processing, with no obligation to maintain coverage. IBM is a hosting vendor that operates the e-business Hosting Environment and processes personal information on Customer's behalf, so this falls squarely within the rule (and no coverage for a vendor processing personal data is walk-away territory). We therefore insert the preferred short insurance paragraph (CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M, workers' compensation, certificates on request) as new Section 14.12A in the general provisions; the E&O 1M / cyber 2M fallback remains available if IBM pushes back on limits.

p0192: Risk of loss for all Base Components shall at all times remain with IBM. Risk of loss for all Customer Components shall at all times remain with Customer.

**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

The Agreement contains no minimum purchase commitment or take-or-pay obligation on Bluefly:

- **§ 4.1 (Charges)** — fees are payable only for Services specified in Service Option Attachments/Order Forms, on a one-time, installment, recurring or usage basis. This is our preferred position: pay for ordered services or actual usage only.
- **§ 11.5 (Capacity Planning)** — allocates capacity-planning responsibility to Customer but sets no committed capacity, volume floor or usage cap.
- **§ 3.4 (Termination for Convenience)** — Customer may exit the Agreement or any individual Service Option Attachment on one month's notice, so even if a commitment were introduced there is a contractual exit.
- Text searches for "minimum", "commit", "shortfall", "take or pay" and "volume" surface nothing else relevant.

One diligence point noted rather than flagged: § 3.4(b) conditions convenience termination on "the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments." None appear in the reviewed text, but we should confirm the attachments carry no minimum-volume or shortfall charge before signature.

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Searches for "minimum", "commit", "shortfall", "take or pay" and "volume" return no purchase-commitment language anywhere in the Agreement. Charges under § 4.1 are payable only for Services specified in Service Option Attachments and Order Forms (one-time, installment, recurring or usage), i.e. for ordered or actual usage only, which is the preferred position. § 11.5 (Capacity Planning) allocates capacity-planning responsibility to Customer but imposes no committed capacity or volume floor, and § 3.4 lets Customer terminate the Agreement or any Service Option Attachment for convenience on one month's notice. The only residual exposure is the reference in § 3.4(b) to "early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments"; no such charges appear in the reviewed text, so there is no take-or-pay without an exit — we would simply confirm on diligence that the attachments contain no minimum-volume or shortfall charge. No redline required.

p0052: Charges for applicable Services will be specified in Service Option Attachments and Order Forms. Charges can be specified as one-time, installment, recurring, or usage. IBM will invoice such Charges when they begin or are due as set forth in Service Option Attachments.
p0044: Customer may terminate this Agreement (including all Service Option Attachments) or any Service Option Attachment (with the exception of any Service Option Attachment that is a prerequisite for the provision of Services under a non-terminated Service Option Attachment) for convenience at the end of any calendar month by:
p0046: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.
p0142: Customer is responsible for determining whether the Base Components, IBM provided Internet access bandwidth, Customer Components and their combination will meet Customer's capacity or performance needs. Customer is responsible for planning for and requesting changes to the Base Components or IBM provided Internet access bandwidth, as determined by Customer, including any additional capacity required to support anticipated peaks in demand that may significantly increase Web site hits, transaction volumes, or otherwise increase system resource utilization.

("Customer"), IBM will provide Web hosting and related services ("Services") to Customer. The Agreement includes these terms and conditions and the documents referenced herein ("Base Terms"), e-business hosting services order forms accepted by IBM ("Order Forms"), and the following attachments:

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

The termination of selected Service Option Attachments will not affect Customer's obligation to pay charges under other Service Option Attachments.
input.rationale: § 3.5 Effect of Termination addresses only Customer's accrued payment obligations. Searches for transition, return, export, deletion and expiration turned up nothing: the only "return" obligations relate to Materials/Base Components on IBM's request (§ 8.1) and returning a signed copy of the Agreement (§ 14.20), and § 14.18 Data Protection is limited to contact-information processing. § 11.6 makes Customer responsible for Content but gives no exit rights. § 14.2 survives § 3.5 but there is no substantive obligation to survive. The Agreement therefore contains no post-termination transition assistance or Content/data return obligation, failing even the fallback (90 days' assistance and export within 30 days), so we insert the preferred exit provision (six months' assistance at then-current rates, machine-readable return within 30 days, then deletion with written certification) into § 3.5, which § 14.2 already preserves post-termination.

reasons: Scope mismatch: § 11.3 is an acceptable-use/content-warranty enforcement right (IBM may investigate suspected unlawful, infringing or abusive Content and then remove/suspend), not a usage or fee-compliance audit. The AUDIT rule is framed around verification of our usage with an underpayment true-up ('independent auditor', 'underpayment exceeds 5%/10%'), so importing it wholesale here misapplies the rule; the absence of any true usage/licence audit right is favourable to us and should not be raised as a deviation.

The imported cost mechanic is incoherent as drafted: 'at IBM's cost unless the investigation reveals an underpayment by Customer exceeding ten percent (10%) of amounts due' has no referent in a § 11.2(b) content-warranty investigation, which cannot produce an underpayment finding. The insertion adds confusing, inoperative language rather than the smallest effective edit.

The redline imposes an absolute 15-day prior written notice condition on any investigation without preserving the existing emergency / 'as required by law' carve-out reflected in § 11.3's notice provision (p0137). As written it would bar IBM from investigating suspected illegal content promptly or where law prohibits tipping off the Customer — an internally inconsistent and non-negotiable position that also invites counterparty rejection of the whole guardrail package.

The once-per-twelve-month frequency cap is unworkable for abuse investigations (it would prevent IBM investigating a second suspected incident in the same year) and is not what the playbook's 'rare, notified, off-site' audit position is designed to address; the confidentiality/independent-investigator and no-system-access asks are the only parts that map sensibly to this clause.

If a comment is warranted at all, it should be a narrower ask (advance notice where practicable, confidentiality obligations on investigators, no access to Customer systems beyond what is necessary), not a full audit-clause template rewrite of an AUP enforcement right.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc.; counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation.

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

input.quote: IBM reserves the right to investigate potential violations of the representations and warranties in Subsection 11.2(b).
input.rationale: § 11.3 is the only right in the Agreement to examine Customer's use of the Services and Content (compliance with the Acceptable Use Policy under § 11.2(b)); there is no other audit, inspection or verification clause (no hits for audit/inspect/verify/records). As drafted the investigation right is unlimited in frequency, requires no advance notice to Customer (the notice in p0137 is only a best-efforts attempt and applies solely before IBM restricts access or removes Content, not before investigating), allocates no cost, imposes no confidentiality on investigators and does not exclude access to Customer systems. That is unlimited and unannounced examination, i.e. walk-away territory, so it fails the fallback on frequency, notice and cost. Redline adopts the fallback (once per twelve months, 15 days' notice, IBM's cost unless underpayment exceeds 10%, no system access) rather than the preferred 30-day/5% formulation, because a 30-day wait would be disproportionate in the context of suspected unlawful Content on IBM-hosted infrastructure.

content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (AUDIT, § 11.3 Suspected Violations).**

- The only Customer-facing examination right in the Agreement is IBM's right in § 11.3 (p0132) to investigate potential violations of the AUP warranty in § 11.2(b). No audit/inspection/verification clause exists elsewhere (searches for "audit", "inspect", "verify", "records", "monitor" returned nothing relevant; §§ 11.5 and 13.2 add no monitoring rights).
- As drafted the right is unlimited in frequency and unannounced — the notice in p0137 is only a best-efforts attempt and applies solely before IBM restricts access or removes Content — with no cost allocation, no confidentiality obligation on investigators and no exclusion of access to our systems. That fails the fallback on all material terms.
- Redline (validated, ok:true) inserts the fallback guardrails into p0132: once per twelve months, 15 days' prior written notice, business hours, independent investigator under confidentiality, IBM's cost unless underpayment exceeds 10%, and no direct or remote access to our systems or Customer Components. We chose the fallback over the preferred 30-day/5% formulation because a 30-day wait would be disproportionate where IBM suspects unlawful Content on its hosted infrastructure.

- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.

Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.

Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.

**Finding submitted: deviation (AUDIT, § 11.3 Suspected Violations).**

- The only Customer-facing examination right in the Agreement is IBM's right in § 11.3 (p0132) to investigate potential violations of the AUP warranty in § 11.2(b). No audit/inspection/verification clause exists elsewhere (searches for "audit", "inspect", "verify", "records", "monitor" returned nothing relevant; §§ 11.5 and 13.2 add no monitoring rights).

That fails the fallback on all material terms.
- Redline (validated, ok:true) inserts the fallback guardrails into p0132: once per twelve months, 15 days' prior written notice, business hours, independent investigator under confidentiality, IBM's cost unless underpayment exceeds 10%, and no direct or remote access to our systems or Customer Components. messages.content:
Verifier feedback: Scope mismatch: § 11.3 is an acceptable-use/content-warranty enforcement right (IBM may investigate suspected unlawful, infringing or abusive Content and then remove/suspend), not a usage or fee-compliance audit. Judge the proposal against the supplied playbook rule, original paragraphs, resolved definitions, deterministic checks, rendered redline, and comment.
Do not rely on hidden drafter reasoning. Fail invalid, directionally wrong, or rule-incomplete edits.
Deterministic checks are heuristics (regular expressions and a changed-character ratio), not verdicts: a failed regex may simply be a phrasing variant, and a high changed-character ratio is acceptable when the rule genuinely requires rewriting the clause (for example replacing a governing-law sentence or deleting a take-or-pay obligation). Weigh them as evidence and decide on substance: does the redline reach the playbook position with the smallest edit that does so, and is the comment accurate?
The claimed status matters: for a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment is expected, and you should pass when the cited text supports compliance. Fail a deviation finding whose cited clause already meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms (the playbook's classification semantics) — a redline that merely upgrades an acceptable fallback to preferred wording is over-flagging. Compliant findings are retained as internal evaluation evidence, not raised as negotiation issues. For deviation or missing findings, require an actionable valid proposal.
Return a concise verdict with actionable reasons.

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
No usage, licence or fee-verification audit right binds Customer anywhere in this Agreement. Searches for "audit", "inspect", "verify", "records" and "monitor" return nothing relevant, and §§ 11.5 (Capacity Planning) and 13.2 (Acceptable Use Policy) give IBM no monitoring or verification rights. § 11.3 is an acceptable-use enforcement right: IBM may investigate suspected breaches of the Content/AUP warranty in § 11.2(b) and then remove Content, restrict access or terminate. It grants no access to Customer systems or records for measuring our usage or charges, so the AUDIT parameters (frequency, notice, cost allocation, underpayment true-up) do not attach to it. Because the complete absence of an audit right is better than the preferred position and benefits Bluefly, the playbook direction rule means this is compliant rather than "missing" or a deviation, and no redline or comment is warranted. On the deterministic "audit frequency limited" check: the miss is expected here, since there is no audit clause capable of carrying a frequency cap, and it is not evidence of an unmet playbook position. Noted for the file only, not as deviations: § 11.3 does not bind investigators to confidentiality or expressly exclude access to Customer systems, and the p0137 notice is best-efforts and attaches only to restriction/removal actions; if § 11.3 is reopened for other reasons we could seek notice where practicable, investigator confidentiality and no access to our systems beyond what is necessary. The suspension and termination remedies in § 11.3(a)-(d) are left to the suspension and termination rules to avoid double-flagging.

p0132: IBM reserves the right to investigate potential violations of the representations and warranties in Subsection 11.2(b). If IBM reasonably determines that a breach of any such warranty has occurred, then IBM may, in its sole and reasonable discretion:

{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — IBM e-business Hosting Agreement (Document: 3.1 Term)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Re:** Playbook review — verified findings, deviations and negotiation posture

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have completed a playbook review of the Agreement. The commercial architecture is broadly workable — the liability cap is symmetrical, Customer has a one-month convenience termination right, IBM gives a genuine IP indemnity carved out of its cap, and there are no exclusivity, non-compete, MFN, minimum-commitment, non-solicitation or audit obligations imposed on us. Those items are compliant and we are not redlining them.

The issues concentrate in five places, three of which we regard as must-fix:

1. **Customer-side indemnity (§ 8.2)** — § 8.2(a)(3) requires us to indemnify IBM for any Services Recipient claim "related, directly or indirectly, to the Services", and § 9.2(a) puts that indemnity outside our cap. This is an uncapped indemnity for IBM's own Services and is walk-away territory.
2. **IP in deliverables (§ 7, § 5.4)** — the default for undesignated Materials is Type II (IBM-owned), with a licence back that does not permit modification or sublicensing, and there is no confirmation that we retain rights in our Content and data.
3. **Liability carve-outs (§ 9.1, § 9.2, § 10)** — the cap basis and mutuality meet the fallback, but there are no carve-outs for confidentiality, gross negligence or wilful misconduct, and § 9.1(c)(2) excludes all liability for loss of or damage to our records or data.

Beyond those, we need to cap the open-ended early termination charges (§ 3.4(b)), fix the at-will revocable licence and Affiliate scope (§ 12.1), bring auto-renewal within the fallback (§ 3.2), add a conformance warranty and remedy (§ 5.1/§ 5.4), insert transition assistance and data return at exit (§ 3.5), add mutual assignment rights (§ 14.10), add a New York venue (§ 14.3), and add an insurance clause (§ 14 general provisions).

Two findings did not clear verification and are carried as **needs review** pending confirmation: non-solicitation (§ 14.8) and audit rights (§ 11.3). On the substance recorded, both appear to favour us (no restraint on our hiring; no usage-audit right against us), but we should re-confirm before signing off.

---

## 2. Findings table

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 8.2 Indemnification by Customer |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 5.4 Other Disclaimers |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | Deviation | § 9.1 IBM's Limitation of Liability |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 14.10 Assignment |
| 5 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant | § 14.16 Freedom of Action |
| 6 | High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties payable by Customer | Deviation | § 3.4 Termination for Convenience |
| 7 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 12.1 License |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 14.16 Freedom of Action |
| 9 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § 4.1 Charges |
| 10 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | § 4.1 Charges |
| 11 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | Needs review (verification failed) | § 14.8 Personnel |
| 12 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Deviation | § 3.2 Renewal |
| 13 | Medium | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 3.4 Termination for Convenience |
| 14 | Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 3.5 Effect of Termination |
| 15 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 5.1 IBM Representations and Warranties |
| 16 | Low | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Needs review (verification failed) | § 11.3 Suspected Violations |
| 17 | Low | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 14.3 Choice of Law |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 14.12 Risk of Loss |

### Proposed positions on the deviations and gaps

- **§ 8.2 (INDEMN).** IBM's IP indemnity in § 8.1 sits at or above our fallback (patent/trademark/copyright/trade secret, standard exclusions, remedies including credit up to 12 months' charges, carved out of IBM's cap under § 9.1(a)) and we are not redlining it; the absence of breach-of-law, data-breach and wilful-misconduct limbs is noted only. On our side, we narrow § 8.2(a)(3) to our breach of applicable law, leaving the Content/AUP and Customer Components limbs intact. The partial relief in § 8.2(c) for IBM's misconduct does not cure the exposure.
- **§ 7 / § 5.4 (IP).** Flip the default for undesignated Materials to Type I (Customer-owned), extend the Type II licence back to modification and sublicensing for our business purposes, and add a sentence confirming our ownership of Content and data (§ 14.17 grants only expressly specified licences, so silence leaves ownership unconfirmed). The broad licence we grant IBM in Type I Materials is noted but not flagged — it is not an assignment.
- **§ 9 / § 10 (LOL-CAP).** Cap amount and mutuality left untouched (the absent USD 1,000,000 floor is a sub-element short of preferred only). We add a single mutual "Excluded Claims" paragraph (new § 9.3) covering confidentiality/data and security, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement.
- **§ 3.4(b) (LD and T4C).** Cap aggregate early termination charges at three (3) months' recurring Charges for the terminated Services as our sole liability for the termination, and add pro-rata refund of prepaid fees. We keep the favourable one-month notice period; § 3.3's carve-out (no early termination charges where IBM breached) and § 3.5's accrued-payment obligation are left as-is.
- **§ 12.1 (LICENSE).** Add Affiliates and Subcontractors acting on our behalf, and limit revocation to termination for our uncured material breach. Transferability is already satisfied by § 14.10's successor carve-out.
- **§ 3.2 (RENEWAL).** Move to 12-month renewal terms, a 30-day opt-out window, a 60-day IBM reminder and uplift capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%; fallback offer of a 60-day window with a 5% cap.
- **§ 3.5 (TRANSITION).** Insert six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, machine-readable return of Content within 30 days and deletion with written certification. § 14.2 already preserves § 3.5 post-termination.
- **§ 5.1 / § 5.4(c) (WARRANTY).** Add a 90-day conformance and no-malicious-code warranty for Materials with a repair / re-performance / refund remedy, and carve the express warranties out of the "AS IS" disclaimer. The existing care-and-skill language stays.
- **§ 14.10 (ASSIGN).** Add an affiliate/asset-sale carve-out for us and subject IBM's assignment to our consent (not unreasonably withheld) with a competitor bar. There is no change-of-control provision anywhere, and IBM's subcontracting right in § 14.8 is untouched.
- **§ 14.3 (GOVLAW).** New York law is our preferred position; add exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County. The mutual jury-trial waiver (§ 14.4) and two-year limitations period (§ 14.14) are noted, not flagged.
- **Insurance.** Insert a short insurance paragraph (CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M, workers' compensation, certificates on request) as new § 14.12A; fallback E&O 1M / cyber 2M.

---

## 3. Walk-away items

These are the points identified in the findings as walk-away territory. We should not sign without movement on each:

1. **§ 8.2(a)(3) — uncapped Services Recipient indemnity.** We indemnify IBM for third-party claims "related, directly or indirectly, to the Services", excluded from our cap by § 9.2(a). Uncapped exposure for IBM's own Services.
2. **§ 3.4(b) — uncapped early termination charges.** Amount defined only by open cross-reference to Attachment A and the Service Option Attachments, neither of which caps it (Attachment A is not in the reviewed document). Unbounded, it could approach or exceed remaining contract value.
3. **§ 12.1 — expressly "revocable" licence with no stated standard.** IBM may withdraw the licence to the Base Components at will.
4. **§ 3.2 — renewal terms "equal in duration to the previous term".** Permits automatic multi-year renewals where an Order Form specifies a multi-year initial term.
5. **No insurance obligation.** IBM operates the hosting environment and processes personal information on our behalf; the absence of any coverage undertaking is walk-away territory under the rule.
6. **§ 5.1 / § 5.4(c) — warranty position.** No conformance warranty, no warranty period and no remedy, with all Materials "AS IS" and § 5.1 made exclusive by § 5.2; this approaches the walk-away position for deliverables.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** with the three critical items (§ 8.2, § 7/§ 5.4, new § 9.3) presented as a package and flagged as conditions of signature.
2. **Obtain Attachment A and the Service Option Attachments** and confirm they contain no early termination charge, minimum-volume or shortfall charge, and no renewal price mechanism. Our § 3.4(b) and MINCOMMIT conclusions depend on that diligence.
3. **Confirm the two needs-review findings** — non-solicitation (§ 14.8) and audit (§ 11.3). Verification did not pass, so we should re-run the check before treating either as closed. If § 11.3 is reopened for other reasons, we would additionally seek notice where practicable, investigator confidentiality and no access to our systems beyond what is necessary.
4. **Internal fallback authority.** Confirm the deal team is comfortable with the recorded fallbacks: three-month cap on early termination charges; 60-day renewal window with 5% uplift cap; 90-day transition assistance with export within 30 days; E&O 1M / cyber 2M insurance limits.
5. **Sequence the low-severity items** (§ 14.3 venue, § 14.10 mutuality, § 14.12A insurance) as a single administrative markup to keep the critical negotiation clean.
6. **Internal note only (do not raise):** if IBM later proposes a non-solicit, hold to the fallback — mutual, limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches, no no-hire."}

These are the points identified in the findings as walk-away territory. We should not sign without movement on each:

1. **§ 8.2(a)(3) — uncapped Services Recipient indemnity.** We indemnify IBM for third-party claims "related, directly or indirectly, to the Services", excluded from our cap by § 9.2(a). Uncapped exposure for IBM's own Services.
2. **§ 3.4(b) — uncapped early termination charges.** Amount defined only by open cross-reference to Attachment A and the Service Option Attachments, neither of which caps it (Attachment A is not in the reviewed document). Unbounded, it could approach or exceed remaining contract value.
3. **§ 12.1 — expressly "revocable" licence with no stated standard.** IBM may withdraw the licence to the Base Components at will.
4. **§ 3.2 — renewal terms "equal in duration to the previous term".** Permits automatic multi-year renewals where an Order Form specifies a multi-year initial term.
5. **No insurance obligation.** IBM operates the hosting environment and processes personal information on our behalf; the absence of any coverage undertaking is walk-away territory under the rule.
6. **§ 5.1 / § 5.4(c) — warranty position.** No conformance warranty, no warranty period and no remedy, with all Materials "AS IS" and § 5.1 made exclusive by § 5.2; this approaches the walk-away position for deliverables.
